subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution:
The correct answer is '**many**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage is referring to the multiple areas within Noida and Ghaziabad.
 
• The appropriate adjective should be used to describe a large number of countable entities (areas).
 
• "**Many**" fits well as it denotes a large number and is used with countable nouns, aligning with the context of the sentence.
 
• Other options ("**lot**", "**very**", "**much**") do not match the grammatical and contextual needs of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

Complete Passage: *Days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Ghaziabad priority **section__** of the Delhi-Meerut Rapid Rail Transit System (RRTS), the **__residents__** of high-rise societies in the National Capital Region called for direct **__connectivity__** to the public transport service points. The residents in **__many__** areas of Noida and Ghaziabad said they would be forced to continue **__relying__** on private vehicles without proper connectivity to the RRTS and **__other__** public transport modes. "The RRTS is a great development; we want **__better__** connectivity to key points like Metro stations, railway stations, Delhi, and the RRTS. **__Without__** any proper public transport, many residents are forced to opt **__for__** a personal car," the president of the New Era Flat Owners Welfare Association, Abhishek Kumar,**__stated__**. The 17-km priority section of the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS corridor was inaugurated by PM Modi on October 7, and it started commercial operations on the next day.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Lot (बहुत): "Lot" can be used to describe a large quantity but is usually accompanied by "a" (e.g., a lot of people) and doesn't fit grammatically here.
 
• Very (बहुत): "Very" is an adverb used to emphasize an adjective or another adverb, but it does not fit here as it lacks a noun to modify.
 
• Much (बहुत): "Much" is used with uncountable nouns, and "areas" is a countable noun.
